description: MIDI to CV interface for note, controller, clock and transport messages, with eight assignable controller outputs

outputs.text: Pitch of the current note at a volt per octave, MIDI note 60 giving 0V, with the global pitch bend added; one, four or eight channels depending on the play mode
10V while a note is held and 0V otherwise, with one channel per voice or per tracked MIDI channel
The note's MIDI velocity mapped from 0 to 127 onto 0 to 10V, held after the gate falls
The value of that output's assigned controller number, 0 to 127 mapped onto 0 to 10V
A 10V, 1ms pulse for every incoming MIDI clock tick, which is 24 of them to the quarter note
A 10V, 1ms pulse every so many MIDI clock ticks, the count set on the menu and starting at 24, which gives one pulse to the quarter note
10V after a MIDI start or continue message and 0V after a stop

notes: nothing comes out until a MIDI driver and device are chosen in the module's menu; the display shows the play mode and the MIDI channel being received.
a note-on at velocity zero is treated as a note-off, controller 123 lowers every gate, and a MIDI stop lowers every gate and takes the run output low.
Multitrack and Matriceal read one note per MIDI channel and switch the input to Omni when they are chosen; check that Omni is set after loading a patch.
menu: Play Mode: Mono, Poly, Chord, Multitrack, Matriceal — sets how incoming notes are spread across the voice outputs and how many channels they carry
Chord: unison gate — in Chord mode, makes all eight gate channels go high while any voice is playing rather than each gating on its own
Pitch Bend Range — how far a full pitch bend moves the pitch outputs, one to twelve semitones, starting at two
CLK/n Division — how many MIDI clock ticks pass between pulses on the divided clock output: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 or 24
CC Assignments — one submenu per controller output, choosing which of the 128 MIDI controller numbers it follows; number 123 is kept for all-notes-off and produces no voltage
